text:
morgan: Heads up — support ticket from BrightBox reporting spike of 5xx + timeouts against hosted API starting ~10:11PT. customer sees p95s jump and some 504s.
lia-support: ticket #94213. I grabbed a sample request and got a 504 after ~30s. Customer attached a cURL that runs in a tight retry loop.
samir: do we have tenant id / key? could be auth or billing evaporation causing retries.
lia-support: tenant=brightbox-prod, key ends with ..ZX (redacted). Logs show a burst of 401 then successful auth then steady traffic — but there are lots of back-to-back retries from the client.
kevin: past incidents where retry storms convert to continuous-batching backlog — queue depth saturates and we hit tail timeouts. Can you paste the gateway logs around 10:10-10:20?
lia-support: pasted: ```
INGRESS [10:11:02] tenant=brightbox-prod req_id=abc123 status=401 reason=token_expired
INGRESS [10:11:03] tenant=brightbox-prod req_id=abc124 status=200
INGRESS [10:11:03] tenant=brightbox-prod req_id=abc125 status=200
INGRESS [10:11:04] tenant=brightbox-prod req_id=abc126 status=429 reason=rate_limit
BATCHER [10:11:05] pool=hosted-a backlog=128 depth=512 tail_p95=12.1s
BATCHER [10:11:10] pool=hosted-a backlog=320 depth=1024 tail_p95=18.6s
GATEWAY [10:11:20] enqueue_fail tenant=brightbox-prod reason=queue_full
```
morgan: backlog=320 depth=1024 — that's the kind of knee that generates customer-facing 5xx/timeouts. Are other tenants hitting same pool?
ops-bot: Alert: pool=hosted-a utilization at 98%, queues approaching depth limit. Auto-scale blocked due to reserved capacity flag.
anya: reserved-capacity flag? BrightBox is on standard hosted, not dedicated — check autoscaler config.
kevin: confirmed autoscaler didn't spin up because continuous-batcher pool is at cap for that region (policy: keep at most 3 extra nodes). We also had a recent deploy that lowered the batcher burst buffer.
samir: so sequence: client had token expiry -> rapid retries -> transient 401/200s -> retry spiral -> enqueues fill continuous batcher -> queue depth hits limit -> gateway starts 503/504ing tail requests.
lia-support: customer was also getting auth refresh errors in their logs — looks like behind-the-scenes token refresh occasionally failing then clients immediately retrying with no backoff (0s).
morgan: mitigation steps we took: 1) temporarily rate-limited brightbox-prod at ingress (throttle 50r/s) 2) lifted reserved-capacity block for pool hosted-a to allow autoscale 3) disabled continuous-batching for that pool for 6 minutes to drain backlog.
ops-bot: Action log: rate-limit applied tenant=brightbox-prod by=morgan at 10:12:05; autoscale policy override applied by=kevin at 10:12:22; continuous-batching toggled OFF for pool=hosted-a by=kevin at 10:12:40.
kevin: after toggling batching off backlog dropped from 320->40 in ~30s, p95 tail dropped from 18s->1.8s, 5xx rate reduced to baseline. Customer confirmed error rate fell.
anya: customer asks for permanent fix — short term we can add ingress retry-slowdown (exponential backoff enforcement), but long term we should: improve token refresh guidance, add client-side recommended backoff in docs, and add a safeguard to the batcher to prefer droppping or rejecting when queue depth is above X instead of amplifying tail latency.
samir: also propose a tenant-level telemetry alert that watches auth-fail spikes and triggers auto-throttle before queue saturation.
lia-support: noted — I'll update support ticket with mitigation and next steps. Customer is ok for now but wants a postmortem.
morgan: assign action items: kevin -> roll a temporary batcher headroom increase (config) for hosted-a; anya -> update docs and notify SDK team to add jitter/backoff sample; samir -> alert rule + runbook for auth-failure->throttle.
kevin: will open PR for headroom change and a follow-up to revert if not needed.
ops-bot: Closing note: incident marked as mitigated at 10:12:58. Please add to incidents board for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
lia-support: thanks — filing postmortem skeleton now.
